CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ankle injury with pain and swelling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Jerry is a 45-year-old male who presents with a right ankle injury sustained while playing basketball with his son. Patient went up for a shot when his son collided with him while he was in the air. Patient landed awkwardly, rolling and twisting the ankle. He reports pain on the outside of the ankle with visible bruising and swelling. Patient has difficulty walking and reports the ankle does not feel stable. Patient recently returned to a regular workout routine at the gym and is concerned about disrupting his fitness progress. He also volunteers as a basketball coach starting in April.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies other injuries or systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not documented.

MEDICATIONS
None reported prior to this visit.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home. He plays basketball recreationally with his 10-year-old son, Sean, who also plays basketball competitively. Patient has recently resumed a regular exercise routine at the gym. Patient has dogs at home.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Not documented.
General: Alert and oriented.
Right ankle: Significant swelling on lateral side. Exquisite tenderness over lateral malleolus. Tenderness over medial deltoid region. Skin intact without epidermolysis. Brisk capillary refill noted. No significant malalignment. Patient able to stand but unable to walk without pain due to instability.

RESULTS
Right ankle X-ray (AP, lateral, and oblique views): Displaced lateral malleolus fracture at Weber C level. No evidence of medial or posterior malleolar fractures. Fracture noted as unstable.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Lateral malleolar fracture, right ankle, Weber C, displaced and unstable.
- Surgical intervention recommended: Open reduction internal fixation with plate and screw placement
- Crutches provided
- Non-weight bearing status
- Activity restrictions for approximately 3 months; patient cleared to continue coaching beginning in April
- Medications: Meloxicam prescribed for pain and swelling management
- Ice therapy and elevation recommended; patient works from home and can elevate ankle regularly
- Orthopedic surgery referral implied for surgical planning and scheduling
